passages.t: The City of Truth, full of old and young
passages.happening:
The chapter opens with God's words, “I am jealous for Zion with great zeal; I am jealous for her with great fervor” (verse 2). He will return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem, which will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of Hosts the Holy Mountain (verse 3).

‘Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age’ (verse 4), and the streets will be full of boys and girls playing (verse 5). If this seems impossible to the remnant, should it seem impossible to God (verse 6)? He will save his people from the east and the west and bring them home, ‘where they will be My people, and I will be their faithful and righteous God’ (verse 8).
passages.hearers:
Chapter 8 is a string of short promises, nearly all opening with this is what the LORD of Hosts says. They answer the sad questions of chapter 7 with joy.

In 518 BC Jerusalem was thinly settled and its walls were broken. The promise of old people sitting in the streets and children playing there is a picture of ordinary peace: a city safe enough for the old to grow old and the young to play. Jealous here means God's fierce, protective love for his people.

Verse 8 renews the covenant words, God's people and their God, with faithfulness and righteousness on God's side.
passages.later: Jeremiah gave the same covenant promise: ‘They will be My people, and I will be their God’ (Jeremiah 32:38). Isaiah spoke of the old and the young in a renewed Jerusalem (Isaiah 65:20).
passages.asks: God's picture of a restored city is old people at rest and children at play. Ask what that says about what God values. And ask what seems impossible to you that may not be impossible to God.

passages.t: Let your hands be strong, and fasts become feasts
passages.happening:
God tells the builders, ‘let your hands be strong’ (verse 9). Before the foundation was laid there were no wages and no safety, but now he will not deal with them as before (verses 10-11). The seed will grow, the vine will bear and the sky will give its dew (verse 12). As they were a curse among the nations, so he will save them and they will be a source of good. ‘Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong’ (verse 13).

As God once resolved to bring disaster, so now he has resolved to do good to Jerusalem and Judah (verses 14-15). ‘Speak truth to one another, render true and sound judgments in your gates’ (verse 16), and do not plot evil or love false oaths (verse 17).

The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months will become times of joy and gladness, ‘Therefore you are to love both truth and peace’ (verse 19). Many peoples will come to seek the LORD in Jerusalem (verses 20-22). In those days ten people from every language will take hold of a Jew's robe and say they want to go with him, because they have heard that God is with his people (verse 23).
passages.hearers:
The four fasts mourned the stages of Jerusalem's fall: the breach of the wall, the burning of the temple, the murder of Gedaliah and the beginning of the siege. God promises to turn every one of them into a feast.

The command in the middle matters. The joy depends on truth and justice in the gates, where courts met. The answer to the question of chapter 7 is now complete: God will turn mourning into joy, and his people are to love truth and peace.

The chapter ends with the nations. Ten is a round number for many. People of every language will hold on to a Jew's robe, because God is with his people. The hope that began with Abraham, that all nations would find good through his family, comes into view.
passages.later: God promised Abraham that all the families of the earth would be reached through him (Genesis 12:3). Isaiah foresaw the nations streaming to the LORD's house (Isaiah 2:2-3).
passages.asks: God promises to turn the fasts into feasts. Ask what grief you are carrying that you need God to turn into joy. And the nations come because they have heard that God is with his people. Ask what people see of God's presence in yours.
